row: A sales journal is used to record?
Cash sales go to the cash receipts journal.
The total of the subsidiary ledger must be:
It is used to check accuracy.
Which transaction is recorded in the general journal?
It is collected on behalf of the government.
a group of accounts with a common characteristic, such as one account for each customer
the general ledger's list of all accounts
a journal used only for cash receipts
Examples: the accounts receivable and accounts payable subsidiary ledgers.
The general ledger account that summarises a subsidiary ledger is called a
Accounts Receivable in the general ledger controls the customer accounts.
At the end of the period, the total of the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger must equal
the Accounts Receivable control account balance
Subsidiary totals must agree with the control account.
Credit sales of merchandise are recorded in the
The sales journal records only credit sales of merchandise.
All receipts of cash, including cash sales and collections from customers, are recorded in the
Every transaction that increases cash goes to the cash receipts journal.
Purchases of merchandise on credit are recorded in the
The purchases journal records credit purchases of inventory.
Payments of cash, such as paying a supplier, are recorded in the
Every transaction that decreases cash goes to the cash payments journal.
A sales return made on account (not for cash) is usually recorded in the
Transactions that fit no special journal go to the general journal.
A main advantage of special journals is that they
save time by grouping similar transactions and posting column totals
remove the need for a general ledger
eliminate the need for source documents
Totals are posted once a month instead of posting every entry.
Under the perpetual system, the monthly total of the Cost of Goods Sold/Inventory column in the sales journal is posted as a
debit to Cost of Goods Sold and a credit to Inventory
debit to Inventory and a credit to Cost of Goods Sold
debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Sales
debit to Cash and a credit to Inventory
Each credit sale also records the cost of the goods sold.
Which of the following is **NOT** one of the three basic principles of an effective accounting information system?
The three principles of accounting information systems are cost-effectiveness, usefulness, and flexibility. Conservatism is an accounting valuation constraint.
A general ledger account that summarizes the total of all individual accounts in a subsidiary ledger is called a:
A control account (such as Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable in the general ledger) summarizes the balances of its corresponding subsidiary ledger.
Which of the following is an advantage of using subsidiary ledgers?
Frees the general ledger from excessive detail and allows division of labor
Eliminates the need for a trial balance
Eliminates the need to record journal entries
Replaces the need for bank reconciliations
Subsidiary ledgers keep individual customer/vendor details out of the general ledger, provide up-to-date individual balances, and enable multiple employees to work simultaneously.
Which special journal is used to record **only credit sales of merchandise inventory**?
The Sales Journal exclusively records sales of merchandise on account. Cash sales go to the Cash Receipts Journal.
When a company receives cash from a customer paying off an account receivable (within the discount period), in which journal is the transaction recorded?
All receipts of cash—including customer collections on account—are recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal.
In a single-column **Purchases Journal**, which transactions are recorded?
All purchases of merchandise on account
All purchases of office equipment on account
A single-column Purchases Journal records only credit purchases of merchandise inventory.
Which journal is used to record the return of defective merchandise purchased on account (when the buyer receives a credit memo from the supplier)?
Purchase returns and allowances on account do not involve cash and are not purchases or sales, so they are recorded in the General Journal.
How often are individual entries affecting customer balances in the **Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger** posted from the Sales Journal and Cash Receipts Journal?
Subsidiary ledger postings are made daily so management always knows the current balance owed by each individual customer.
How often are the column totals of special journals (such as Accounts Receivable Dr. / Sales Cr.) posted to the **General Ledger**?
Monthly (at the end of the month)
Summary column totals in special journals are posted to the General Ledger at the end of each month.
In the Cash Receipts Journal, why is an **X** placed below the total of the **"Other Accounts Cr."** column at month-end?
Because the column total is not posted to the general ledger (items were already posted individually)
To indicate an error in addition
Because the items belong in the subsidiary ledger
To show the column was audited
Items in the "Other Accounts" column affect different general ledger accounts and are posted individually during the month; posting the total would double-count them.
A company sells old office equipment on account (not merchandise) to an employee. In which journal should this transaction be recorded?
The Sales Journal is strictly for credit sales of merchandise inventory. Credit sales of plant assets are recorded in the General Journal.
When a company establishes a petty cash fund by writing a check for $300, in which journal is this entry recorded?
Establishing or replenishing a petty cash fund involves a cash disbursement (writing a check), which is recorded in the Cash Payments Journal.

At the end of the month, the **Accounts Payable** control account in the General Ledger has a credit balance of $28,400. The Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger contains three vendor balances: Vendor X ($10,200), Vendor Y ($9,500), and Vendor Z. What must Vendor Z's credit balance be?
The sum of subsidiary ledger balances must equal the control account: $28,400 - $10,200 - $9,500 = $8,700.
In the **Cash Payments Journal**, which of the following columns would normally be included?
Inventory Cr. (for purchase discounts taken under a perpetual system)
Under a perpetual system, when paying suppliers within the discount period, the Cash Payments Journal debits Accounts Payable, credits Inventory (for the discount), and credits Cash.
A check mark (✓) in the Reference (Ref.) column of a Sales Journal next to a customer's name indicates that:
The amount has been posted to the customer's account in the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger
The amount has been posted to the General Ledger
Because subsidiary ledger accounts do not have account numbers, a check mark (✓) is placed in the Ref. column to show the item was posted to the subsidiary ledger.
A customer returns merchandise that was originally purchased on credit, and the seller issues a credit memo. In which journal does the **seller** record this transaction?
Sales returns and allowances on account are recorded by the seller in the General Journal.
What is the dual posting requirement when an entry in the **General Journal** affects Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable?
Post to BOTH the General Ledger control account and the individual Subsidiary Ledger account
Post only to the General Ledger
Post only to the Subsidiary Ledger
Post at the end of the year only

When a General Journal entry involves AR or AP, it must be posted to both the GL control account (recording the account number) and the individual subsidiary ledger account (recording a check mark ✓) so the two ledgers stay in agreement.
In a multi-column **Purchases Journal**, a company purchases $1,200 of store supplies on account. How is this posted?
Individually to Store Supplies in the GL and individually to the vendor in the AP Subsidiary Ledger
Only at month-end to the General Ledger
Only to the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger
It is not posted until paid in cash

In a multi-column Purchases Journal, items in the "Other Accounts Dr." column (like Store Supplies) are posted individually to the GL, and the credit to AP is posted individually to the vendor's AP subsidiary ledger.
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems differ from basic manual special journals primarily because ERP systems:
Integrate all business functions (accounting, sales, manufacturing, HR) into a single centralized database
Eliminate the need for financial statements
Are only suitable for small sole proprietorships
ERP systems integrate accounting with all operational departments in one unified database, automating journal entries and ledger updates.

A company uses a Sales Journal, Purchases Journal, Cash Receipts Journal, Cash Payments Journal, and General Journal. On May 12, the company receives a $5,000, 60-day, 6% promissory note from Customer A to settle an overdue open account receivable. In which journal is this recorded?

Accepting a note receivable in exchange for an account receivable involves no cash and is not a sale of inventory, so it is recorded in the General Journal (Dr. Notes Receivable / Cr. Accounts Receivable).
On May 25, Customer A pays off the $5,000 note plus $50 interest in cash. In which journal does the company record this cash collection?
Any receipt of cash (including collection of a note receivable and interest) is recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal.

In a perpetual inventory system, the **Sales Journal** has two money columns: Accounts Receivable Dr. / Sales Revenue Cr. and Cost of Goods Sold Dr. / Inventory Cr. At the end of June, the totals are $84,000 and $52,000 respectively. How are these totals posted?
Posted at month-end to four General Ledger accounts: Dr. AR $84,000, Cr. Sales $84,000, Dr. COGS $52,000, Cr. Inventory $52,000
Marked with an X and not posted
Posted only to the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger
Special journal column totals are posted at month-end to their respective General Ledger accounts.

During June, a bookkeeper mistakenly posted a $650 credit sale from the Sales Journal to the General Ledger Accounts Receivable control account (via the monthly total), but **forgot** to post the $650 debit to Customer B's individual account in the **Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger**. What will happen at month-end?
The General Ledger Trial Balance will still balance, but the AR Control Account will exceed the sum of the AR Subsidiary Ledger by $650
The General Ledger Trial Balance will not balance by $650
The AR Subsidiary Ledger will exceed the AR Control Account by $650
The General Ledger debits and credits are equal so the trial balance balances, but the AR Control Account is $650 higher than the sum of individual customer balances in the subsidiary ledger.
Which of the following transactions is recorded in the **Cash Payments Journal**?
Paying a supplier $2,940 cash (after a $60 purchase discount) to settle a $3,000 account payable
Purchasing merchandise on account from Supplier K
Returning damaged goods to Supplier K for credit
Paying cash to settle an account payable is a cash disbursement recorded in the Cash Payments Journal.
A company sells merchandise for $1,500 cash (cost $900) under a perpetual inventory system. In which journal is this recorded, and which columns are used?
Cash Receipts Journal: Cash Dr. $1,500, Sales Cr. $1,500, and COGS Dr. $900 / Inventory Cr. $900
Sales Journal: AR Dr. / Sales Cr.
General Journal: Cash Dr. $1,500, Sales Cr. $1,500
Cash Receipts Journal: Cash Dr. $1,500, Accounts Receivable Cr. $1,500
Cash sales are recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal with debits to Cash and COGS, and credits to Sales Revenue and Inventory.
What is the purpose of the **Account Numbers** written in parentheses (112) (401) beneath a column total in a special journal?
To indicate that the column total has been posted to those General Ledger accounts
To show the date of the transaction
To indicate that the column total should NOT be posted
To show the number of transactions on the page
Writing the GL account numbers in parentheses under a special journal column total confirms that the total has been posted to those General Ledger accounts.
A company uses a single-column Purchases Journal (for credit purchases of merchandise inventory only). Where should the company record a $4,500 purchase of **office equipment on account**?
When a company uses a single-column Purchases Journal restricted to merchandise inventory, credit purchases of plant assets or supplies must be recorded in the General Journal.
In the **Cash Receipts Journal**, a company receives $8,000 cash from issuing common stock (or owner investment). Where is the $8,000 credit recorded?
In the Other Accounts Cr. column, and posted individually to the General Ledger
In the Accounts Receivable Cr. column
In the Sales Revenue Cr. column

Non-routine cash receipts (such as issuing stock, borrowing on a note, or selling equipment for cash) are entered in the Other Accounts Cr. column of the Cash Receipts Journal and posted individually to the GL.

At April 30, the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger shows balances for:
• Alpha Co.: $3,200 (debit)
• Beta Co.: $4,800 (debit)
• Gamma Co.: $400 (credit — due to an overpayment)
What should be the balance of the **Accounts Receivable Control Account** in the General Ledger?
Net subsidiary ledger total = $3,200 + $4,800 - $400 = $7,600 debit. (Note: On the balance sheet, the $400 credit balance is reclassified as a current liability/customer advance.)
Which of the following sequences represents the correct order of phases in developing an accounting information system?
The four system development phases are: (1) Analysis, (2) Design, (3) Implementation, and (4) Follow-up.
If an entry in the **General Journal** is Dr. Accounts Payable — Delta Supply $600 / Cr. Inventory $600 (for a purchase return), what appears in the Ref. column of the General Journal after posting?
Both 201 / ✓ on the Accounts Payable line, and 120 (GL Inventory) on the Inventory line
Because Accounts Payable affects both the GL control account (201) and Delta Supply's subsidiary ledger (✓), both references are recorded on that line.
Which special journal would **NEVER** have a column for Cash?
The Sales Journal records only credit sales of merchandise, so Cash is never involved.
In a multi-column **Purchases Journal**, the total of the Accounts Payable Cr. column at month-end is $47,300. This total is posted as a:
Credit to Accounts Payable in the General Ledger
Debit to Accounts Payable in the General Ledger
Credit to each individual supplier in the Subsidiary Ledger
Debit to Inventory in the General Ledger
The monthly total of Accounts Payable Cr. is posted as a credit to the Accounts Payable control account in the General Ledger.
Why does a manual accounting system use special journals instead of recording every transaction in a single two-column General Journal?
Special journals reduce repetitive writing and drastically cut down the number of postings to the General Ledger
Special journals eliminate the need for double-entry accounting
Special journals prevent all human arithmetic errors
Special journals are required by tax law
Special journals allow one-line entries for routine transactions and batch-posting of monthly totals to the General Ledger, saving substantial time and labor.

A company accidentally footed (totaled) the Sales Journal column as $54,900 instead of the true sum of $59,400, and posted $54,900 to the General Ledger (Dr. AR $54,900 / Cr. Sales $54,900). Individual customer accounts were posted correctly. How will this error be detected?
The sum of the AR Subsidiary Ledger will exceed the GL AR Control Account by $4,500
The General Ledger Trial Balance will be out of balance by $4,500
The GL AR Control Account will exceed the AR Subsidiary Ledger by $4,500
Cash will be out of balance
Individual customer accounts received the true $59,400 total, while the GL control account only received $54,900, leaving the subsidiary ledger $4,500 higher than the control account.
Which of the following is a **Control Account**?
Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable are the two most common General Ledger control accounts supported by subsidiary ledgers.
In a computerized accounting system, what replaces the manual posting of special journal totals at the end of the month?
Software modules (Sales, Purchasing, Cash) automatically update both the subsidiary records and the General Ledger in real time or upon batch approval
Nothing; users must still post manually at month-end
Only the General Journal is used
Computerized systems automatically post transactions simultaneously to subsidiary ledgers and General Ledger control accounts.
When a company pays a $500 cash dividend to shareholders, in which special journal is the transaction recorded?
Paying cash dividends is a cash disbursement, so it is recorded in the Cash Payments Journal (Dividends Dr. in Other Accounts / Cash Cr.).
At the end of the month, a bookkeeper verifies that the schedule of Accounts Payable subsidiary balances equals the Accounts Payable control account balance. This procedure is an example of:
Reconciling subsidiary ledger schedules with General Ledger control accounts verifies the accuracy and completeness of accounting records.

A bookkeeper recorded a $1,200 cash collection from Customer M in the **Cash Receipts Journal**, entering $1,200 in Cash Dr. and $1,200 in Sales Revenue Cr. instead of Accounts Receivable Cr. What is the effect of this error?
Sales Revenue and Accounts Receivable are both overstated by $1,200
The Trial Balance will be out of balance by $1,200
Crediting Sales Revenue instead of AR overstates Sales Revenue by $1,200 and fails to reduce Accounts Receivable (leaving AR overstated by $1,200), while the trial balance still balances.

In the **Purchases Journal**, the total of the Accounts Payable Cr. column at month-end is $62,500. When posting to the General Ledger, the bookkeeper accidentally posted $62,500 as a **debit** to Accounts Payable instead of a credit, while properly debiting Inventory for $62,500. By how much will the General Ledger **Trial Balance** be out of balance?
Posting a $62,500 credit as a debit creates a discrepancy of 2 × $62,500 = $125,000 (Total Debits exceed Total Credits by $125,000).
Which of the following transactions would be split across **two different journals** (e.g., Cash Receipts Journal and General Journal) in a manual system?
Selling merchandise for $5,000 where the customer pays $1,500 cash down and signs a $3,500 promissory note for the balance
Selling merchandise for $5,000 on open account
Collecting $5,000 cash on an existing account receivable
The $1,500 cash down payment is recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal, while the $3,500 promissory note is recorded in the General Journal (using a clearing mechanism so sales aren't double-counted).

At May 31, the Accounts Receivable control account in the General Ledger has a balance of $45,200, while the schedule of Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger totals $44,750. Which of the following errors explains this $450 discrepancy?
A $450 sales return in the General Journal was posted to the GL Accounts Receivable control account, but was **not** posted to the customer's subsidiary account
A $450 cash sale was omitted from the Cash Receipts Journal
A $450 credit sale in the Sales Journal was posted to the customer's subsidiary account as $900 instead of $450
A $450 purchase on account was posted to Accounts Receivable
Crediting the customer's subsidiary account reduced the subsidiary schedule by $450 (to $44,750), while omitting the credit to the GL AR control account left it at $45,200.

When a company uses a **voucher register** (which replaces the Purchases Journal) and a **check register** (which replaces the Cash Payments Journal), every approved obligation is recorded first in the:
Voucher Register (Dr. Asset/Expense / Cr. Vouchers Payable)
In a voucher system, all approved obligations (whether paid immediately or later) are entered in the Voucher Register as a credit to Vouchers Payable, and then paid via the Check Register.
Why is Vouchers Payable in a voucher system a replacement for the traditional Accounts Payable account?
Unpaid vouchers filed in order of due date serve as the subsidiary ledger, eliminating a separate AP subsidiary ledger
It eliminates the need to pay suppliers
The file of unpaid vouchers organized by payment due date acts directly as the subsidiary record for Vouchers Payable.

In a **Cash Receipts Journal**, the columns are: Cash Dr., Sales Discounts Dr., Accounts Receivable Cr., Sales Revenue Cr., and Other Accounts Cr. Which mathematical equality must hold true on every page before posting?
Cash Dr. + Sales Discounts Dr. = Accounts Receivable Cr. + Sales Revenue Cr. + Other Accounts Cr.
Cash Dr. - Sales Discounts Dr. = Accounts Receivable Cr.
Accounts Receivable Cr. = Sales Revenue Cr.
Cross-footing verifies that total debit column totals equal total credit column totals (Cash Dr. + Sales Discounts Dr. = AR Cr. + Sales Cr. + Other Cr.).
A company collects a $10,000 note receivable plus $300 interest in cash. In the Cash Receipts Journal, how is this entered?
Cash Dr. $10,300; Other Accounts Cr.: Notes Receivable $10,000 and Interest Revenue $300 (two lines)
Recorded in the General Journal only
Because Notes Receivable and Interest Revenue do not have dedicated columns, both are entered on separate lines in the Other Accounts Cr. column and posted individually to the General Ledger.
Which internal control benefit is directly provided by **cross-footing** special journals at the end of each month?
It proves that total debits equal total credits in the journal before posting to the General Ledger
Cross-footing checks that the sum of all debit column totals equals the sum of all credit column totals, preventing unbalanced postings to the GL.
What happens if a bookkeeper posts the total of the Other Accounts Cr. column in the Cash Receipts Journal to a Miscellaneous Revenue account in addition to posting the individual items?
Total credits will exceed total debits on the General Ledger Trial Balance
Total debits will exceed total credits on the General Ledger Trial Balance
The Trial Balance will still balance
Posting the Other Accounts total in addition to individual postings double-counts the credits, causing total credits to exceed total debits.
In an accounting information system, which document typically triggers the recording of a **credit sale** in the Sales Journal?
Sales Invoice accompanied by a Shipping Document (Bill of Lading)
A sales invoice supported by proof of shipment (bill of lading) verifies that goods were shipped and revenue can be recorded.
Which document is compared against the supplier's invoice and the purchase order before approving a voucher for payment?
Receiving Report (confirming quantities and condition of goods actually received)
The three-way match compares the Purchase Order, Receiving Report, and Vendor Invoice before approving payment.

A company uses a multi-column **Cash Payments Journal** with columns: Other Accounts Dr., Accounts Payable Dr., Inventory Cr., and Cash Cr. If the company pays $1,800 cash to purchase equipment, which columns are used?
Other Accounts Dr. (Equipment) $1,800 and Cash Cr. $1,800
Accounts Payable Dr. $1,800 and Cash Cr. $1,800
Cash purchases of equipment are entered in Other Accounts Dr. (posted individually to Equipment) and Cash Cr..
Which of the following statements about **Subsidiary Ledgers** is **FALSE**?
Subsidiary ledger accounts are included directly on the General Ledger Trial Balance
They can be maintained for Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Equipment, and Inventory
Every subsidiary ledger must have a corresponding Control Account in the General Ledger
Subsidiary ledgers allow different clerks to post to customer and vendor records simultaneously
Only the General Ledger Control Account balance appears on the General Ledger Trial Balance; subsidiary ledger balances are summarized in a separate schedule.
Why would a company use a **Sales Returns and Allowances Journal** in addition to the five standard journals?
Because the volume of sales returns is so high that a dedicated special journal improves efficiency
Because GAAP prohibits recording sales returns in the General Journal
To avoid deducting returns from Sales Revenue
To record cash refunds to customers
Companies add extra special journals (like a Sales Returns Journal) whenever a specific type of transaction occurs frequently enough to justify one.
In a General Ledger account, what is written in the Ref. column when an entry is posted from **page 7 of the Cash Receipts Journal**?
Posting references use the journal abbreviation and page number (CR7 = Cash Receipts Journal, page 7).
If a company's accounting system fails to separate the person who enters vendor invoices into the Purchases Journal from the person who approves cash payments, what fraud risk is created?
Creating fictitious "shell" vendors and issuing company checks to oneself
Without segregation between invoice entry/approval and check signing, an employee can set up fake suppliers and approve fraudulent disbursements.
What is the primary role of an **audit trail** in an accounting information system?
To allow transactions to be traced forward from source documents to financial statements and backward from financial statements to source documents
To eliminate the need for bank reconciliations
To prevent all customer bad debts
Posting references, document numbers, and journal page numbers create an audit trail for verifying transaction validity.
When an adjusting entry is recorded at month-end to accrue $800 of salaries payable, which journal is used?
All adjusting entries are recorded in the General Journal.
At year-end, the Equipment control account in the General Ledger has a debit balance of $240,000, while the Plant Asset Subsidiary Ledger cards total $235,000. What is the most likely cause?
A $5,000 equipment purchase was posted to the General Ledger control account but omitted from the Plant Asset Subsidiary Ledger
A $5,000 equipment purchase was omitted from both ledgers
Posting the $5,000 debit purchase to the GL control account raised it to $240,000, while omitting it from the subsidiary ledger left the subsidiary cards at $235,000.
Which of the following are the four primary functional stages/components of data processing in an Accounting Information System (AIS)?

An AIS captures Input (source documents), performs Process (recording/posting/calculating), generates Output (financial statements/reports), and maintains Storage (ledgers/databases). องค์ประกอบหลักของ AIS คือ Input, Process, Output และ Storage
In an Accounting Information System, a barcode scanner at a retail checkout counter and a sales invoice are examples of which AIS component?
Barcode scanners and source documents (invoices, receipts) capture raw transaction data as Input into the AIS. เครื่องสแกนบาร์โค้ดและเอกสารต้นทางเป็นอุปกรณ์/เอกสารฝั่ง Input
Which of the following is an example of an Output component in an AIS?
Printed Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Aging Schedule displayed on a monitor
Financial statements, management reports, and customer statements produced for users are Output. งบการเงินและรายงานต่างๆ ที่แสดงผลให้ผู้ใช้คือ Output
In a computerized AIS, cloud servers, magnetic hard drives, and General Ledger database files serve primarily as which AIS component?
Database files, servers, and ledgers retain accounting records for future retrieval and audit, representing Storage. ฐานข้อมูลและแฟ้มบัญชีแยกประเภททำหน้าที่เป็น Storage
Accounting software algorithms that automatically sort transactions, compute totals, and post entries from journals to ledgers represent which AIS component?
Classifying, calculating, summarizing, and posting data transform inputs into outputs during the Process stage. การคำนวณ จัดหมวดหมู่ และผ่านรายการคือขั้นตอน Process
Which of the following is NOT one of the three basic principles of an effective Accounting Information System?
The three AIS design principles are cost-effectiveness, usefulness, and flexibility. หลักการออกแบบ AIS 3 ข้อคือ คุ้มค่าต้นทุน (Cost-effectiveness), มีประโยชน์ (Usefulness) และยืดหยุ่น (Flexibility)
Which special journal is used exclusively to record credit sales of merchandise inventory?
Only sales of merchandise on account are entered in the Sales Journal. สมุดรายวันขาย (Sales Journal) ใช้บันทึกเฉพาะการขายสินค้าเป็นเงินเชื่อเท่านั้น
In which journal are all cash sales and all collections from customers on account recorded?
Every transaction involving the receipt of cash is recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal. รายการรับเงินสดทุกประเภทบันทึกลงในสมุดรายวันรับเงิน
A company uses a single-column Purchases Journal. Which transaction is recorded in this journal?
Purchase of merchandise inventory on account
Purchase of merchandise inventory for cash
Purchase of delivery truck on account
Return of defective merchandise to a supplier
A single-column Purchases Journal records only credit purchases of merchandise inventory.
All disbursements of cash by check (such as paying suppliers on account, paying rent, or establishing petty cash) are recorded in the:
All cash outflows are recorded in the Cash Payments Journal. รายการจ่ายเงินสดทุกประเภทบันทึกลงในสมุดรายวันจ่ายเงิน
Which of the following transactions must be recorded in the General Journal?
Adjusting entries, closing entries, and sales/purchase returns on account
Cash payment of monthly utility bill
Non-routine transactions that do not fit into any special journal—including adjusting, closing, and returns on account—go into the General Journal.
A General Ledger account (such as Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable) that summarizes the total balance of an entire subsidiary ledger is called a:

A control account in the General Ledger equals the sum of all individual accounts in its related subsidiary ledger. บัญชีคุมยอด (Control account) ในสมุดแยกประเภททั่วไปต้องมียอดรวมเท่ากับบัญชีแยกประเภทย่อยทั้งหมด
How frequently are individual transactions posted to the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger and Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger?
Subsidiary ledger postings are made daily so management knows exact customer and vendor balances at any time. ผ่านรายการไปบัญชีแยกประเภทย่อยเป็นรายวัน
How frequently are the special column totals of special journals posted to the General Ledger?
Monthly (at the end of each month)
Column totals in special journals are posted to General Ledger accounts at month-end. ยอดรวมของช่องเฉพาะในสมุดรายวันเฉพาะจะผ่านรายการไปสมุดแยกประเภททั่วไปตอนสิ้นเดือน
Why is an X placed below the total of the "Other Accounts" column in the Cash Receipts Journal and Cash Payments Journal?
Because the column total is NOT posted to the General Ledger (each item was already posted individually)
Because the column contains mathematical errors
Because the items are posted to the subsidiary ledger
Items in "Other Accounts" are posted individually during the month; posting the column total would duplicate them.

At the end of the month, the Accounts Receivable control account has a debit balance of $34,500. The subsidiary ledger contains three customers: Customer A ($12,400), Customer B ($14,100), and Customer C. What must Customer C's balance be?
A check mark (✓) in the Ref. column of a Sales Journal next to a customer's entry indicates that:
The amount has been posted to the customer's individual account in the AR Subsidiary Ledger
The amount was posted to the General Ledger
Subsidiary ledger accounts are arranged alphabetically without account numbers, so a ✓ confirms posting to the subsidiary ledger.
Under a perpetual inventory system, which columns appear in the Sales Journal?
Accounts Receivable Dr. / Sales Revenue Cr. and Cost of Goods Sold Dr. / Inventory Cr.
Sales Discounts Dr. / Accounts Receivable Cr.
Under a perpetual system, the Sales Journal records both the selling price (AR Dr. / Sales Cr.) and the cost (COGS Dr. / Inventory Cr.) on a single line.
When a General Journal entry involves Accounts Receivable (e.g., a sales return on account), where must it be posted?
To BOTH the General Ledger Accounts Receivable control account AND the customer's individual AR Subsidiary Ledger account
Only to the General Ledger Accounts Receivable control account
Only to the customer's account in the AR Subsidiary Ledger
Neither ledger until cash is received
Dual posting keeps the GL control account and the subsidiary ledger in agreement.
Which of the following is a major benefit of using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software?
It integrates accounting with sales, inventory, purchasing, and HR in one centralized database
It eliminates the need for double-entry accounting
It removes all internal control requirements
ERP systems centralize all organizational data and automate accounting entries across departments.

Match the following AIS items to their correct functional category (Input, Process, Output, Storage):
1. Touch-screen Point-of-Sale (POS) terminal scanning customer items
2. Database server storing the General Ledger and Subsidiary Ledgers
3. Monthly Bank Reconciliation and Balance Sheet printed for management
POS scanner = Input; Database server = Storage; Printed reports/statements = Output.
Which of the following is a source document used as Input in the revenue/collection cycle?
Customer sales invoice and remittance advice
Sales invoices (for credit sales) and remittance advices (accompanying customer payments) are primary source documents for Input.
In an AIS, a Central Processing Unit (CPU) executing accounting software rules to validate journal entries and update account balances performs which function?
Validating, calculating, sorting, and updating ledgers occur in the Process component.
Which of the following is an Output document sent externally to customers at the end of each month to verify their account balances?
Monthly customer statements are external Output documents generated from the Accounts Receivable Subsidiary Ledger.
When designing an Accounting Information System, ensuring that the system can easily expand to handle new product lines, branch offices, and increased transaction volume reflects which principle?
Flexibility allows an AIS to adapt to organizational growth and changing information requirements.
A company sells merchandise for $2,000 cash and $3,500 on account in two separate transactions. In which journals are these two transactions recorded?
$2,000 in the Cash Receipts Journal; $3,500 in the Sales Journal
$2,000 in the Cash Payments Journal; $3,500 in the General Journal
Both in the Cash Receipts Journal
Cash sales go to the Cash Receipts Journal; credit sales of merchandise go to the Sales Journal.
Which transaction would be recorded in the Cash Payments Journal?
Paying $3,920 cash (net of $80 discount) to settle a $4,000 account payable
Receiving a $4,000 check from a customer
Recording a $400 purchase allowance granted by a supplier
Paying cash to settle an account payable is a cash disbursement recorded in the Cash Payments Journal.

In a multi-column Purchases Journal (with columns for Accounts Payable Cr., Inventory Dr., Supplies Dr., and Other Accounts Dr.), a company buys $3,000 of store equipment on account. How is this posted?
Accounts Payable Cr. is posted daily to the vendor's AP Subsidiary Ledger (and monthly via total to GL); Equipment Dr. is posted individually to the GL
Posted only at month-end as part of column totals
Recorded in the Cash Payments Journal instead

In a multi-column Purchases Journal, items in Other Accounts Dr. are posted individually to the GL, while Accounts Payable Cr. is posted daily to the vendor subsidiary account and monthly via the column total to the GL control account.

What happens if a bookkeeper posts a $500 credit sale from the Sales Journal to the customer's individual account in the AR Subsidiary Ledger, AND includes it in the monthly Sales Journal total posted to the General Ledger, AND ALSO posts the $500 individually to the General Ledger Accounts Receivable control account?
The GL Accounts Receivable control account will exceed the AR Subsidiary Ledger by $500, and the GL Trial Balance will be out of balance by $500
The GL Trial Balance will still balance, and nothing is wrong
The AR Subsidiary Ledger will exceed the GL control account by $500
Posting $500 individually to the GL AR control account in addition to the monthly column total double-debits GL Accounts Receivable by $500.
Which of the following transactions is recorded in the General Journal?
Issuing a credit memo to a customer for returned merchandise originally sold on credit
Collecting a note receivable in cash
Sales returns and allowances on account are recorded in the General Journal.
In the Cash Receipts Journal, cross-footing confirms that:
Cash Dr. + Sales Discounts Dr. = Accounts Receivable Cr. + Sales Revenue Cr. + Other Accounts Cr.
Sales Revenue Cr. = Cost of Goods Sold Dr.
All transactions occurred on the same day
Cross-footing verifies that total debit column sums equal total credit column sums on every journal page.

When a company records a $750 purchase return on account in the General Journal (Dr. Accounts Payable—Apex Co. $750 / Cr. Inventory $750), what is entered in the Ref. column on the Accounts Payable line after posting?
201 / ✓ (both the GL control account number and the subsidiary ledger check mark)
General Journal entries affecting AR or AP require dual posting to both the GL control account (201) and the subsidiary ledger (✓).
Which of the following is NOT a General Ledger Control Account?
Equipment (when supported by a plant asset subsidiary ledger)
Customer Jones is an individual subsidiary ledger account, not a General Ledger control account.
In a manual AIS, what does the posting reference CP12 in a General Ledger account mean?
CP12 stands for Cash Payments Journal, page 12 (CR = Cash Receipts, S = Sales, P = Purchases, G = General).
Why do companies use subsidiary ledgers?
To keep excessive individual detail out of the General Ledger, enable division of labor, and quickly identify errors
To eliminate the need for a General Ledger
Because tax authorities forbid recording customer names in any ledger
Subsidiary ledgers streamline the General Ledger and allow multiple accounting clerks to update individual customer/vendor accounts simultaneously.

A company accidentally footed (added) the Purchases Journal column as $38,200 instead of the correct total of $32,800, and posted $38,200 to the General Ledger (Dr. Inventory $38,200 / Cr. Accounts Payable $38,200). Individual vendor accounts were posted accurately. What will occur at month-end?
The GL Accounts Payable control account will exceed the AP Subsidiary Ledger schedule by $5,400, while the GL Trial Balance still balances
The GL Trial Balance will be out of balance by $5,400
The AP Subsidiary Ledger will exceed the GL control account by $5,400
Equal debits and credits ($38,200) were posted to the GL so the trial balance balances, but GL Accounts Payable is $5,400 higher than the sum of individual vendor accounts.
Which business document proves that ordered goods have physically arrived at the company's warehouse in good condition?
The Receiving Report documents quantities and condition of incoming shipments.
In a computerized accounting system, what is a relational database?
A collection of structured tables (customers, vendors, inventory, transactions) linked by primary and foreign keys to eliminate data redundancy
A paper notebook used for petty cash
Relational databases link master files and transaction files without duplicating customer or product data.
If a company receives a $4,000 cash refund from a supplier for returned merchandise that had already been paid for, in which special journal is this recorded?
Receiving cash is always recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal (Cash Dr. / Inventory Cr. in Other Accounts).
What is the final phase of developing an Accounting Information System, during which management monitors the new system to verify it meets user needs and fixes any operational issues?
The four phases are Analysis → Design → Implementation → Follow-up.

In an e-commerce Accounting Information System, trace the exact sequence of AIS components when a customer orders online:
1. Customer clicks "Checkout" and enters credit card details on website
2. System checks inventory availability, calculates sales tax, and updates AR/Cash and Inventory tables
3. Transaction record is written to the cloud SQL database
4. Electronic receipt is emailed to customer and daily sales summary is displayed on manager's dashboard
Data entry = Input; calculations & ledger updates = Process; writing to SQL database = Storage; emailed receipt & dashboard = Output.
Which of the following devices can function as BOTH an Input device and an Output device in a modern Point-of-Sale (POS) AIS?
A touchscreen POS terminal accepts cashier/customer touch entries (Input) and displays item prices, totals, and prompts (Output).
Which of the following is an internal source document generated within the company to initiate the purchase of needed inventory?
A Purchase Requisition is an internal Input document requesting the purchasing department to order goods.
In a computerized AIS, master files (such as the Customer Master File and Inventory Master File) correspond to which component of a manual accounting system?
Master files store permanent and cumulative balances for individual customers, vendors, and inventory items—just like subsidiary ledgers.
Which of the following transactions requires entries in BOTH the Accounts Receivable control account and a customer's subsidiary account, and in which journal is it recorded?
Credit sale of merchandise → Sales Journal
Cash sale of merchandise → Cash Receipts Journal
Purchase of supplies on account → Purchases Journal
Payment of rent by check → Cash Payments Journal
Credit sales in the Sales Journal debit individual customer accounts daily and debit the GL AR control account via the monthly total.

A company sells merchandise for $6,000, receiving $2,000 cash down and a $4,000, 60-day promissory note for the balance. If the company uses standard special journals, how is this transaction recorded without double-counting Sales Revenue?
Enter $2,000 in Cash Receipts Journal (Cash Dr. / AR Cr.) and enter the full $6,000 sale in General Journal (Dr. AR $2,000, Dr. Notes Receivable $4,000 / Cr. Sales Revenue $6,000)
Enter $6,000 in both the Sales Journal and Cash Receipts Journal
Using Accounts Receivable as a clearing bridge between the General Journal and Cash Receipts Journal records the full $6,000 sale once while capturing the $2,000 cash receipt in the CRJ.

At May 31, the Accounts Payable control account in the General Ledger has a credit balance of $52,000, while the schedule of Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger totals $53,400. Which error explains this $1,400 difference?
A $1,400 purchase return in the General Journal was posted to the GL Accounts Payable control account, but was omitted from the vendor's subsidiary account
A $1,400 credit purchase in the Purchases Journal was omitted from the vendor's subsidiary account
A $1,400 cash payment to a vendor was omitted from both ledgers
A $700 credit purchase was posted to the GL control account twice

Debiting the GL control account for the $1,400 return reduced the GL balance to $52,000, while forgetting to debit the vendor's subsidiary account left the subsidiary schedule $1,400 higher ($53,400).
In a Cash Payments Journal, what happens if the bookkeeper posts the total of the "Other Accounts Dr." column to Miscellaneous Expense in addition to posting the individual items in that column?
Total debits will exceed total credits on the General Ledger Trial Balance
Total credits will exceed total debits on the General Ledger Trial Balance
The Trial Balance will still balance
Posting the "Other Accounts Dr." total double-counts those debits, causing total debits on the GL Trial Balance to exceed total credits.
Which of the following is TRUE regarding a Voucher System?
Every approved cash expenditure requires a pre-numbered voucher recorded in the Voucher Register before a check is issued in the Check Register
It eliminates the need to verify receiving reports
It is only used for recording credit sales
A voucher system enforces strict authorization and documentation prior to every cash disbursement.

A company uses a single-column Sales Journal (credit sales of merchandise) and a single-column Purchases Journal (credit purchases of merchandise). In which journal is a credit purchase of office supplies recorded?
Single-column Purchases Journals only accommodate credit purchases of merchandise inventory; credit purchases of supplies or equipment go in the General Journal.

In a manual AIS, when a bookkeeper posts an individual entry from the "Other Accounts Cr." column of the Cash Receipts Journal to the General Ledger Notes Receivable account (Account #115), what is written in the Ref. column of the Cash Receipts Journal?
Writing the GL account number (115) in the Ref. column confirms that the line item was posted individually to that General Ledger account.

Which control procedure in an AIS ensures that data entered into a computerized input screen is complete, accurate, and within valid ranges (e.g., rejecting a negative quantity or non-existent customer ID)?
Automated input edit checks (field checks, limit checks, validity checks) prevent invalid data from entering the AIS.
Which of the following errors will be immediately caught by cross-footing the Cash Receipts Journal?
A $500 cash receipt was entered as $500 in Cash Dr. and $50 in Accounts Receivable Cr.
A $500 cash collection from Customer A was accidentally credited to Customer B's subsidiary account
A $500 cash sale was never recorded at all
A $500 check was stolen before reaching the accounting department
Cross-footing compares total debit columns against total credit columns on the journal page, immediately catching an unequal entry ($500 Dr. vs. $50 Cr.).
What is the purpose of a Chart of Accounts in an AIS?
To provide a structured numeric coding system of all General Ledger accounts (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenues, Expenses)
To list all employees and their salaries
The Chart of Accounts organizes and numbers all General Ledger accounts for systematic recording and reporting.
If a company grants a customer a $250 cash refund for returned merchandise, in which special journal is this recorded?
A cash refund to a customer is a cash disbursement recorded in the Cash Payments Journal (Sales Returns & Allowances Dr. in Other Accounts / Cash Cr.).
Which of the following is NOT a benefit of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems?
Zero implementation cost and instant setup
Real-time financial reporting across global subsidiaries
Elimination of duplicate data entry across departments
Standardized business processes and automated controls
ERP systems are expensive and complex to implement, though they provide major long-term operational and reporting benefits.
In a General Ledger Accounts Receivable control account, the debit posting at month-end from page 4 of the Sales Journal will show which reference?
When is batch processing preferred over real-time processing in an AIS?
For periodic, scheduled tasks such as biweekly payroll runs or monthly depreciation entries
When instant inventory availability is needed at an online checkout
Batch processing groups similar transactions together for scheduled processing (like payroll or monthly depreciation).

At year-end, the Accounts Receivable control account is $80,000. Customer A owes $35,000, Customer B owes $47,000, and Customer C has a $2,000 credit balance due to an overpayment. How should this be presented on the classified balance sheet?
Accounts Receivable $82,000 (Current Asset) and Credit Balances in Customers' Accounts $2,000 (Current Liability)
Material credit balances in customer accounts represent liabilities and must be reclassified as a Current Liability ($2,000), leaving gross debit AR at $82,000.
Which system development activity involves training employees, converting historical files, and testing the new accounting software before going live?
Staff training, data conversion, and system testing occur during the Implementation phase.
